sourceBaseline.interpretation: The monolith ranking query is compatibility authority for this pure resolver: active joined assignments, exclusive expiry, Free Plan seed and minimum valid ranking candidate. Conflicting grace, scheduling, direct-grant, token-claim and PlanFeatures behavior remains unresolved rather than invented.

targetBase.interpretation: Immutable completed post-A2.6 snapshot before adding the pure entitlement-snapshot resolver.

invariants.claim: Resolution is a pure function of one caller-supplied epoch-microsecond observed_at and never reads a process clock or mutable external state.
Only an active assignment joined to a present active plan contributes ranking entitlement candidates.
An assignment is current only when expiry is absent or strictly later than observed_at; equality is expired.
Every relevant metadata or ranking-permission candidate is parsed without lossy casts and strictly range-validated; decimal permission suffixes retain source-compatible leading-zero semantics.
Inactive permissions and permission strings outside the exact ranking-offset namespace do not affect a snapshot result.
The selected offset starts at the Free Plan value and can only move to the minimum valid effective candidate.
NoEffectivePlan, EffectivePlansWithoutGrant and PlanGrant successes remain distinct, including a PlanGrant whose value is exactly 100.
Reordering input rows or repeating equivalent join rows cannot change the resolved entitlement outcome.
Malformed relevant snapshot data returns an error and is never represented as an empty snapshot or successful Free Plan decision.
The pure resolver is not wired into the identity gRPC runtime; the active binary fails closed with ServiceUnavailable until authoritative entitlement wiring exists.
A2.7 applies neither assigned_at scheduling nor grace; both require a later explicit backend authority decision.
All proof is local and hermetic and authorizes no database, RPC, browser, listener, deployment or production action.

residualStops.claim: Core still owns plans, assignments and permissions; no reviewed core-owned adapter supplies an entitlement snapshot to identity.
No one-statement or transactionally consistent owner-scoped SQL snapshot has been implemented or proven.
Schema compatibility, version-ledger adoption, populated upgrade and source reconciliation remain unproved.
The identity gRPC runtime returns Unavailable until the authoritative entitlement adapter is wired; this resolver remains unactivated.
Scheduled-start and grace behavior conflict across source surfaces and are deliberately unresolved by A2.7.
Direct permissions, token claims and PlanFeatures are not ranking authority in A2.7 and require a later explicit decision.
The identity RPC has no authenticated workload identity, exact caller authorization, owner binding or TLS policy.
Ranking changes have no transactional outbox, monotonic revision, durable cursor, replay or gap-repair contract.
No typed BFF or Dioxus UI consumes this resolver and no browser loading, free, paid, stale or error flow is proven.
No live fixture parity, shadow read, staging, observability, mismatch alert or rollback evidence exists.
Route ownership, immutable images, configuration, gateway, Kubernetes, canary, rollback and deployment remain unchanged.
Passing A2.7 integrity is not production readiness and never authorizes a live service, database, secret or deployment action.

requiredExecutionOrder: E01 freeze source semantics and the immutable post-A2.6 target base
E02 implement the pure fixed-observed-at snapshot resolver
E03 replay the deterministic fixture ledger through exact hermetic tests
E04 preserve fail-closed runtime wiring and every non-production boundary
E05 add a reviewed core-owned atomic snapshot adapter and schema proof
E06 reconcile scheduling, grace, direct grants, token claims and PlanFeatures authority
E07 wire authenticated identity RPC plus durable revision and replay semantics
E08 prove typed BFF and UI behavior against reconciled local fixtures
E09 obtain separate live parity, shadow, canary, rollback and deployment authorization
